cds.title: University of Central Florida Common Data Set 2025-2026 (PDF)

cost.notes: First-year, full-time costs for the full 2026-27 year from the Common Data Set (G1). Tuition $6,368 in-state, $26,732 out-of-state/nonresident ($212.28 and $891.07 per credit hour, 30 credits); G1 reports required fees as $0; on-campus food and housing $12,436 (housing $6,496 + meal plan $5,940). Estimated expenses (G5, residents): books $1,200, transportation $1,094, other $3,104 (other costs shown = transportation + other). UCF's admissions cost page (2026-27, based on 28 credit hours) lists different figures: tuition and fees $5,954 for Florida residents and $22,482 for non-residents, housing $8,750, food $6,170. For the I-20, UCF Global states $44,291 per year for undergraduates: tuition and fees $21,456 (12 credits per semester), living expenses $20,318, mandatory health insurance $2,517. Institutional aid for nonresidents is non-need-based only (CDS H6): 328 degree-seeking undergraduate nonresidents received aid, average $994 (2024-25 final data).

stats.notes: From the Common Data Set (Fall 2025 entering class): 59,629 applied, 25,522 admitted (42.8%), 8,103 enrolled; the residency rows (in-state / out-of-state / international) add up to the totals. International first-years: 2,365 applied, 575 admitted (24.3%), 156 enrolled, so the international admit rate is far below the in-state rate (21,823 of 46,049). Waitlist: 2,966 offered a place, 2,157 accepted, 343 admitted. No early decision; non-binding early action exists (CDS: closing date 10/15, notification 12/4) but the CDS gives no early-action counts. Average GPA above 4.0 means UCF reports a weighted/recalculated GPA; the GPA table is the 'all enrolled students' column (the rows add to 99.9% from rounding; 0.0% below 2.50) and 100% of enrollees had a GPA reported. Test submission is the share of enrolled first-years: 73.9% SAT, 25.8% ACT (CDS C9). Undergraduate enrollment (60,083) and the nonresident count (2,171) are the 'Total Undergraduates' figures (they include non-degree-seeking students such as dual enrollment). Class rank: 33% in the top tenth, 68% in the top quarter (76% reported rank).
